dashboardPageTitle.description: Browser tab title for the dashboard page. "Byte Budget" is the product name and is not translated.

dashboardBrandEyebrow.description: Product name, shown above the page heading. Leave untranslated; it is the extension's name.

dashboardBrandTitle.description: Main heading (h1) of the dashboard page.

dashboardLoading.description: Placeholder under the page heading, replaced by the period description as soon as figures arrive.

dashboardPeriodGroupLabel.description: Accessible name for the Session/Today/7 days/30 days picker in the page header.

dashboardNavLabel.description: Accessible name for the two-link nav that switches between Dashboard and Settings.

dashboardNavSettings.description: Navigation link to the settings page.

dashboardOverviewLabel.description: Accessible name for the region holding the four stat cards at the top of the page.

dashboardStatDataUsed.description: Label of the stat card showing total bytes for the chosen period.

dashboardMeasuredPill.description: Small badge on the "Data used" card. The share of the total that was measured from real response sizes rather than estimated. Not a claim of overall accuracy — see dashboardMeasuredPillTitle.

dashboardMeasuredPillTitle.message: Response bodies measured. Header overhead is estimated and halved, WebSocket frames are invisible to an extension, and a cancelled body counts as zero — see How Byte Budget measures usage.
dashboardMeasuredPillTitle.description: Tooltip on the measured badge. It deliberately lists what the measured percentage does NOT cover, so the badge cannot be read as "the total is exact". The closing phrase names the disclosure section on the same page (dashboardMethodSummary); translate it the same way there.

dashboardStatTopSite.description: Label of the stat card showing the heaviest site of the period.

dashboardTopSiteNoUsage.description: Hint under the "Top site" card when nothing has been recorded in this period.

dashboardStatProjected.description: Label of the stat card showing where the cycle is expected to end up. Always this word, whatever the card's value says, because the figure is modelled rather than measured.

dashboardProjectedNoPlan.description: Value of the "Projected" card when no plan size has been set, so there is nothing to project against.

dashboardProjectedNoPlanHint.description: Hint under the "Projected" card when no plan size has been set.

dashboardProjectedSetPlanLink.message: Set your plan size and reset day
dashboardProjectedSetPlanLink.description: Link on the "Projected" card that opens the settings page.

dashboardProjectedNotYet.description: Value of the "Projected" card when a plan exists but no day of the cycle has finished, so no rate can be computed.

dashboardProjectedNotYetHint.message: No day of this cycle has finished
dashboardProjectedNotYetHint.description: Hint under the "Projected" card when the cycle has only just begun.

dashboardProjectedTooEarly.description: Value of the "Projected" card when too few days have finished for the projection to be stated. No figure is printed at all in this state.

dashboardProjectedTooEarlyHint.message: Too few finished days to state a figure
dashboardProjectedTooEarlyHint.description: Hint under the "Projected" card when the projection is not confident enough to print.

dashboardProjectedOverPlan.description: Hint under the "Projected" card when the projection lands above the plan size.

dashboardProjectedUnderPlan.description: Hint under the "Projected" card when the projection lands below the plan size.

dashboardProjectionBasis.description: Line under the stat cards saying what rate the projection assumed and over what window. The basis text comes from the worker and is already a sentence fragment describing the rate.

basis.example: 1.2 GB a day over the 6 finished days of this cycle

dashboardProjectionSpentOn.message: The plan was already spent, on $DAY$.
dashboardProjectionSpentOn.description: Second sentence of the projection basis line when the plan ran out on a day that has already passed. This date was found by reading recorded days, so it is measured rather than modelled.

dashboardProjectionRunsOutOn.message: At that rate it runs out on $DAY$.
dashboardProjectionRunsOutOn.description: Second sentence of the projection basis line when the plan is expected to run out on a future day. "At that rate" marks it as modelled, unlike dashboardProjectionSpentOn.

dashboardStatDataPrevented.description: Label of the stat card showing bytes that were never transferred. "Prevented", not "saved": these bytes are not part of the total on the neighbouring card, so the two do not share a denominator.

dashboardPreventedHintSplit.message: $MEASURED$ of it measured, the rest modelled
dashboardPreventedHintSplit.description: Hint under the "Data prevented" card. The card's own figure is a sum of a measured subtraction and an estimate, and this says how much of it is which. The distinction must survive translation: "measured" is arithmetic on sizes on file, "modelled" is a guess.

dashboardPreventedHintCache.description: Hint under the "Data prevented" card when nothing was prevented but the browser cache avoided some traffic. The leading tilde marks the figure as approximate; keep it or use the local equivalent.

dashboardPreventedHintNone.message: Turn on Data Saver or add a limit
dashboardPreventedHintNone.description: Hint under the "Data prevented" card when nothing has been prevented and nothing is set up to prevent anything. "Data Saver" is a feature name used throughout the product.

dashboardComparisonSame.message: About the same as the previous $WINDOW$
dashboardComparisonSame.description: Note under the "Data used" card when this period matches the one before it. The window word is one of dashboardWindowSession/Day/Week/SevenDays/Month/ThirtyDays.

dashboardComparisonMore.description: Note under the "Data used" card when this period used more than the one before it. Separate from dashboardComparisonLess so the direction is never a substituted fragment.

dashboardComparisonLess.description: Note under the "Data used" card when this period used less than the one before it. Separate from dashboardComparisonMore so the direction is never a substituted fragment.

dashboardWindowSession.description: Names the window a period-over-period comparison is against. Substituted into dashboardComparisonSame/More/Less, e.g. "18% less than the previous session". Lower case, mid-sentence.

dashboardWindowDay.description: Names the window a period-over-period comparison is against. Substituted into dashboardComparisonSame/More/Less, e.g. "18% less than the previous day". Lower case, mid-sentence.

dashboardWindowWeek.description: Names the window a comparison is against when weeks are counted as calendar weeks. Substituted into dashboardComparisonSame/More/Less. Lower case, mid-sentence.

dashboardWindowSevenDays.description: Names the window a comparison is against when a week means the last 7 days rather than a calendar week. Substituted into dashboardComparisonSame/More/Less. Lower case, mid-sentence.

dashboardWindowMonth.description: Names the window a comparison is against when months are counted as calendar months. Substituted into dashboardComparisonSame/More/Less. Lower case, mid-sentence.

dashboardWindowThirtyDays.description: Names the window a comparison is against when a month means the last 30 days rather than a calendar month. Substituted into dashboardComparisonSame/More/Less. Lower case, mid-sentence.

dashboardStaleNote.description: Notice in the page header when the figures on screen are older than the refresh interval, so a stale number is never presented as live.

dashboardSitesTitle.description: Heading of the panel listing sites by bytes used.

dashboardSiteSearchLabel.description: Search box above the site list. Used as both the placeholder and the accessible name, which must stay identical, so it is one message.

dashboardSitesEmpty.message: No usage yet. Browse normally and sites will appear here.
dashboardSitesEmpty.description: Empty state of the site list when nothing has been recorded for the chosen period.

dashboardSitesFilteredCount.description: Count beside the site list while a search filter is active: how many sites match out of how many exist.

dashboardSiteCountOne.description: Count beside the site list, singular. Chrome's message format has no plural rules, so the singular and plural are separate whole messages.

dashboardSiteCountOther.description: Count beside the site list, plural. Paired with dashboardSiteCountOne.

dashboardShowAllSites.description: Button at the foot of the site list revealing the rows past the first 25. Only ever shown with a count above 25, so no singular form is needed.

dashboardReservedRowTitle.message: Requests that did not belong to a tab: browser services, service workers and other extensions.
dashboardReservedRowTitle.description: Tooltip on the site row for the reserved ledger buckets, which are not real sites.

dashboardOpenSiteDetails.description: Tooltip on a site row, saying that clicking it opens the detail panel.

dashboardSiteShareOfTotal.description: Second figure on a site row: this site's share of the period's total.

dashboardSiteShareOfTotalEstimated.description: Second figure on a site row when under three quarters of the site's bytes were measured. Separate whole message rather than a suffix appended to dashboardSiteShareOfTotal, so the qualifier can be placed wherever the language needs it.

dashboardDetailTitle.description: Heading of the panel that opens when a site row is clicked.

dashboardDetailClose.description: Button that closes the site detail panel.

dashboardAnnounceSiteDetails.description: Announced to a screen reader when the detail panel opens or swaps to another site.

dashboardErrorReadSite.description: Announced when the detail panel's request to the background worker fails.

dashboardDetailIncludesEstimates.description: Qualifier in the detail panel's summary line when under 90% of the site's bytes were measured.

dashboardPageLoadCountOne.description: Number of recorded page loads for a site, singular.

dashboardPageLoadCountOther.description: Number of recorded page loads for a site, plural. Paired with dashboardPageLoadCountOne.

dashboardDetailVisitsSummary.description: Part of the detail panel's summary line: how many page loads were recorded and the median bytes of one. "Typical" is the median, not the mean.

dashboardDetailLimitHeading.description: Heading of the block in the detail panel for setting a data limit on the site.

dashboardDetailWindowLabel.description: Label for the Session/Day/Week/Month picker that chooses which window a limit's allowance covers.

dashboardDetailShapeLabel.description: Label for the picker that chooses what happens once a limit's allowance is spent.

dashboardDetailSaverHeading.description: Heading of the block in the detail panel for turning Data Saver on or off for this site. "Data Saver" is the product's name for the optimizer feature.

dashboardDetailHoursHeading.description: Heading and chart caption for the site's hourly usage chart.

dashboardDetailDaysHeading.description: Heading and chart caption for the site's daily usage chart.

dashboardTypeOfData.description: Heading and chart caption for the breakdown by resource type — video, images, scripts and so on. Used for the panel on the overview and for the block inside the detail panel.

dashboardDetailHostsHeading.description: Heading of the table listing the hostnames a site's bytes actually came from.

dashboardHostsColumnHost.description: Column header in the source hosts table: the hostname.

dashboardHostsColumnData.description: Column header in the source hosts table: bytes transferred.

dashboardHostsColumnRequests.description: Column header in the source hosts table: number of requests.

dashboardHostsOff.message: Per-host detail is switched off, so nothing was recorded to show here.
dashboardHostsOff.description: Empty state of the source hosts table when the user has turned per-host recording off. Distinct from dashboardHostsEmpty: nothing was ever recorded, rather than nothing happened.

dashboardHostsEmpty.message: No host detail for this period yet.
dashboardHostsEmpty.description: Empty state of the source hosts table when per-host recording is on but this period has no rows. Distinct from dashboardHostsOff.

dashboardHostThirdParty.description: Tag beside a hostname in the source hosts table when the host is not part of the site itself. Lower case: it is a tag, not a sentence.

dashboardChartNothingRecorded.description: Shown in place of a chart when the series is empty.

dashboardPreventedLabel.description: Names the second band drawn inside each bar of the daily chart, in the key, in the bar tooltips and in the chart's screen-reader summary. Not "saved": those bytes were never transferred, so they are not part of the bar they sit inside. "Partly estimated" is not optional — the figure is a measured subtraction plus a size model's guess. Lower case, used mid-phrase.

dashboardTrendTitle.description: Heading of the panel holding the daily usage chart.

dashboardTrendCaption.description: Caption read out with the daily usage chart, naming the range currently shown.

dashboardRangeGroupLabel.message: Range for the daily chart and the Data Saver results
dashboardRangeGroupLabel.description: Accessible name for the 2 weeks/30 days/3 months picker. It names both panels because the control also re-scopes the Data Saver results far below the fold.

dashboardRangeTwoWeeks.description: Option in the range picker, and the range name substituted into dashboardTrendCaption and dashboardRangeAnnouncement.

dashboardRangeThirtyDays.description: Option in the range picker, and the range name substituted into dashboardTrendCaption and dashboardRangeAnnouncement.

dashboardRangeThreeMonths.description: Option in the range picker, and the range name substituted into dashboardTrendCaption and dashboardRangeAnnouncement.

dashboardRangeAnnouncement.message: Daily usage and Data Saver results now cover the last $RANGE$.
dashboardRangeAnnouncement.description: Announced to a screen reader after the range picker changes, because the second panel it re-scopes is several hundred pixels below the control.

dashboardMethodSummary.description: Summary line of the collapsed disclosure explaining the measurement method. Referred to by name at the end of dashboardMeasuredPillTitle; keep the two the same.

dashboardMethodBodyOne.message: Totals use the best information available from Chrome and each site. If an exact size is unavailable, Byte Budget makes a clearly labelled estimate.
dashboardMethodBodyOne.description: First paragraph of the measurement disclosure.

dashboardMethodBodyTwo.message: The measured percentage covers response bodies and nothing else. Header overhead is counted from the names and values and then halved, because HTTP/2 compresses headers by an amount Chrome does not report; WebSocket frames are invisible to an extension; a cancelled response counts as zero. So 100% measured means every body was measured, not that the total is exact.
dashboardMethodBodyTwo.description: Second paragraph of the measurement disclosure. It is the product's statement of what the measured percentage does and does not cover; the final sentence is the point of the paragraph and must not be softened.

dashboardMethodBodyThree.message: Every figure here covers this Chrome profile. A second profile, another browser, a native app, an operating system update and every other device on the same connection are invisible to an extension — there is no API that would show them. A carrier's figure can be several times larger, and the difference is not an error in this one.
dashboardMethodBodyThree.description: Third paragraph of the measurement disclosure, on why the extension's total differs from a carrier's bill.

dashboardLimitPeriodSession.description: Option in the limit window picker: the allowance covers this browser session. Kept short to fit a segmented control; the longer wording is the button's tooltip.

dashboardLimitPeriodDay.description: Option in the limit window picker: the allowance covers one day. Kept short to fit a segmented control.

dashboardLimitPeriodWeek.description: Option in the limit window picker: the allowance covers one week. Kept short to fit a segmented control.

dashboardLimitPeriodMonth.description: Option in the limit window picker: the allowance covers one month. Kept short to fit a segmented control.

dashboardLimitShapeProgressive.description: Option for what a limit does once the allowance is spent: drop heavy resource types in stages rather than refuse everything. Kept short to fit a segmented control.

dashboardLimitShapeHard.description: Option for what a limit does once the allowance is spent: refuse every subresource at once. Kept short to fit a segmented control.

dashboardLimitWindowSession.description: Names the window a share is a share of, substituted into dashboardLimitStatusFigure, e.g. "42% of this session's limit". Lower case, mid-sentence.

dashboardLimitWindowDay.description: Names the window a share is a share of, substituted into dashboardLimitStatusFigure, e.g. "42% of today's limit". Lower case, mid-sentence.

dashboardLimitWindowWeek.description: Names the window a share is a share of, substituted into dashboardLimitStatusFigure. Lower case, mid-sentence.

dashboardLimitWindowMonth.description: Names the window a share is a share of, substituted into dashboardLimitStatusFigure. Lower case, mid-sentence.

dashboardLimitStatusOver.description: State chip on a site's limit when more than the allowance has been used.

dashboardLimitStatusNearlyFull.description: State chip on a site's limit at 85% or more of the allowance.

dashboardLimitStatusWithin.description: State chip on a site's limit below 85% of the allowance.

dashboardLimitStatusPaused.description: State chip on a site's limit while enforcement is snoozed.

dashboardLimitStatusFigure.description: Line beside the limit's state chip: how much of the allowance is spent and when the window rolls over. The window comes from dashboardLimitWindowSession/Day/Week/Month and the reset clause from dashboardLimitResetsAt or dashboardLimitResetsNever.

dashboardLimitResetsNever.message: runs until this browser session ends
dashboardLimitResetsNever.description: Reset clause for a session limit, which has no rollover time. Substituted into dashboardLimitStatusFigure. Lower case, mid-sentence.

dashboardLimitResetsAt.description: Reset clause for a limit whose window rolls over at a known time. Substituted into dashboardLimitStatusFigure. Lower case, mid-sentence.

dashboardLimitMeterFigure.description: Figure under the limit's progress meter: bytes used against the allowance for the window.

dashboardLimitPausedHint.message: Nothing is being refused while it is paused. Without the pause: $TIER$
dashboardLimitPausedHint.description: Hint under a paused limit that has no known resume time. The tier text describes what would be refused and comes from the shared tier descriptions.

tier.example: Video, audio, images and web fonts are refused.

dashboardLimitPausedHintResumes.message: Nothing is being refused while it is paused; it resumes $WHEN$. Without the pause: $TIER$
dashboardLimitPausedHintResumes.description: Hint under a paused limit that has a resume time. A whole separate message rather than an optional clause spliced into dashboardLimitPausedHint, because a mid-sentence insertion cannot be reordered by a translator.

tier.example: Video, audio, images and web fonts are refused.

dashboardReservedNoLimit.message: These requests have no site of their own for a rule to name, so they cannot be limited individually. A limit over Everything covers them along with the rest.
dashboardReservedNoLimit.description: Shown in place of the limit controls for the reserved ledger buckets, which are not origins. "Everything" is the displayed name of the limit that covers all sites; translate it the same way it is translated there.

dashboardResumeNow.description: Button that ends a paused limit immediately.

dashboardAnnounceLimitResumed.description: Announced to a screen reader after a paused limit is resumed.

dashboardPauseOneHour.description: Button that suspends a limit's enforcement for one hour.

dashboardAnnounceLimitPaused.description: Announced to a screen reader after a limit is paused.

dashboardRemoveLimit.description: Button that deletes the limit on this site.

dashboardAnnounceLimitRemoved.description: Announced to a screen reader after a limit is removed.

dashboardNoLimitHint.message: No limit on this site. A limit refuses requests before they are sent, so the bytes are never spent.
dashboardNoLimitHint.description: Shown in the detail panel when the site has no limit, naming what a limit actually does.

dashboardPresetTitle.description: Tooltip on each round-figure preset button, spelling out the limit the button would create.

dashboardConsequenceHard.message: A hard stop refuses every subresource the moment the allowance runs out. The page's own HTML still loads, so the site can say why it looks broken.
dashboardConsequenceHard.description: Explains what the "Hard stop" shape does. Substituted into dashboardLimitHintReplaces or dashboardLimitHintExact.

dashboardConsequenceProgressive.message: Shedding weight drops video and audio at 60% of the allowance, images and web fonts at 85%, and everything but the page shell at 100%.
dashboardConsequenceProgressive.description: Explains what the "Shed weight" shape does. Substituted into dashboardLimitHintReplaces or dashboardLimitHintExact.

dashboardLimitHintReplaces.message: $CONSEQUENCE$ Choosing a size replaces the current limit on this site.
dashboardLimitHintReplaces.description: Hint under the preset buttons when the site already has a limit. The consequence sentence is dashboardConsequenceHard or dashboardConsequenceProgressive; it is a placeholder rather than a concatenation so the two sentences can be ordered as the language needs.

consequence.example: A hard stop refuses every subresource the moment the allowance runs out. The page's own HTML still loads, so the site can say why it looks broken.

dashboardLimitHintExact.message: $CONSEQUENCE$ For an exact figure, use the limit form in Settings.
dashboardLimitHintExact.description: Hint under the preset buttons when the site has no limit yet. The consequence sentence is dashboardConsequenceHard or dashboardConsequenceProgressive.

consequence.example: A hard stop refuses every subresource the moment the allowance runs out. The page's own HTML still loads, so the site can say why it looks broken.

dashboardAnnounceLimitApplied.description: Announced to a screen reader after a preset button creates or replaces a limit.

dashboardErrorGeneric.description: Fallback shown and announced when a limit action fails and the worker gave no message of its own.

dashboardSaverReserved.message: Data Saver acts on requests belonging to a page, so it does not reach these.
dashboardSaverReserved.description: Shown in place of the Data Saver switch for the reserved ledger buckets, which have no page.

dashboardSaverUnreadable.message: Data Saver settings could not be read.
dashboardSaverUnreadable.description: Shown in place of the Data Saver switch when the settings request to the worker failed.

dashboardSaverOffEverywhere.message: Data Saver is off everywhere. It rewrites image requests to known CDNs so they return a smaller variant, refuses analytics beacons, and defers offscreen images and video. It applies to every site except the ones you exclude, and the switch that turns it on turns it back off.
dashboardSaverOffEverywhere.description: Shown in the detail panel when Data Saver is disabled globally. It names the whole of what the feature does and the whole of how to undo it, rather than selling it.

dashboardSaverOpenSettings.description: Link from the detail panel to the Data Saver section of the settings page.

dashboardSaverOffForSite.description: Label of the per-site Data Saver switch when the site is excluded.

dashboardSaverOnForSite.description: Label of the per-site Data Saver switch when the site is not excluded.

dashboardSaverExcludedHint.message: This site is on the never-optimize list: nothing here is rewritten, deferred or refused by Data Saver. Its page loads are also left out of the comparison table below.
dashboardSaverExcludedHint.description: Hint under the per-site Data Saver switch when the site is excluded.

dashboardSaverIncludedHint.message: Image requests to known CDNs are asked for a smaller variant, analytics beacons are refused, and offscreen images and video wait until they are reached.
dashboardSaverIncludedHint.description: Hint under the per-site Data Saver switch when the site is optimized, saying exactly what is being done to it.

dashboardAnnounceSaverOn.description: Announced to a screen reader after Data Saver is switched on for a site.

dashboardAnnounceSaverOff.description: Announced to a screen reader after Data Saver is switched off for a site.

dashboardErrorSetSiteOptimize.message: Could not change Data Saver for that site.
dashboardErrorSetSiteOptimize.description: Announced when the per-site Data Saver request to the worker fails.

dashboardAdviceNoFeature.message: $SHARE$ of this site's bytes are $TYPE$. Nothing in Data Saver removes $TYPE$, so a limit is the only lever here.
dashboardAdviceNoFeature.description: Recommendation line for a site whose dominant resource type no Data Saver feature touches. The type name is the same word both times.

dashboardAdviceFeatureOn.message: $SHARE$ of this site's bytes are $TYPE$. The Data Saver setting aimed at that is "$FEATURE$", which is on by default.
dashboardAdviceFeatureOn.description: Recommendation line naming the Data Saver feature aimed at this site's dominant resource type, when that feature ships switched on. Separate from dashboardAdviceFeatureOff so "on" is never a substituted fragment. The quotation marks around the feature name may be replaced with the local ones.

dashboardAdviceFeatureOff.message: $SHARE$ of this site's bytes are $TYPE$. The Data Saver setting aimed at that is "$FEATURE$", which is off by default.
dashboardAdviceFeatureOff.description: Recommendation line naming the Data Saver feature aimed at this site's dominant resource type, when that feature ships switched off. Separate from dashboardAdviceFeatureOn so "off" is never a substituted fragment.

dashboardSavingsTitle.description: Heading of the panel reporting what Data Saver prevented.

dashboardSavingsRangeButton.description: Button in the Data Saver results panel that sends focus up to the range picker, which scopes both panels.

dashboardManageSaverLink.description: Link from the Data Saver results panel to the Data Saver section of the settings page.

dashboardSavingsMeasuredLabel.description: Label of the left savings tile. This figure is arithmetic: the original size was on file and the smaller version's cost is subtracted from it. It must not be phrased the same way as dashboardSavingsEstimatedLabel — the whole point of the pair is that one is a subtraction and the other is a guess.

dashboardSavingsMeasuredHint.message: Original sizes on file, minus what the smaller version cost
dashboardSavingsMeasuredHint.description: Hint under the Measured savings tile, stating the arithmetic. Its figure carries no tilde, unlike the Estimated tile, because nothing about it is approximate.

dashboardSavingsEstimatedLabel.description: Label of the right savings tile. This figure is the size model's guess for requests refused before any size was known. Its value is printed with a leading tilde meaning "approximately". It must not be phrased the same way as dashboardSavingsMeasuredLabel: merging the two into one figure is the one thing this panel exists to prevent.

dashboardSavingsEstimatedHint.message: The size model's guess for requests refused before they had a size
dashboardSavingsEstimatedHint.description: Hint under the Estimated savings tile. "Guess" is deliberate and should stay a word that admits uncertainty; the tile's tilde says the same thing in punctuation.

dashboardRequestsRefusedOne.description: Count of requests Data Saver refused in the window, singular.

dashboardRequestsRefusedOther.description: Count of requests Data Saver refused in the window, plural. Paired with dashboardRequestsRefusedOne.

dashboardRequestsSmallerOne.description: Count of requests Data Saver rewrote to a smaller variant, singular.

dashboardRequestsSmallerOther.description: Count of requests Data Saver rewrote to a smaller variant, plural. Paired with dashboardRequestsSmallerOne.

dashboardOriginalSizesOne.description: Count of un-rewritten resource sizes recorded, which is what makes the measured saving a subtraction rather than a guess. Singular.

dashboardOriginalSizesOther.description: Count of un-rewritten resource sizes recorded. Plural; paired with dashboardOriginalSizesOne.

dashboardSavingsHintOff.message: Data Saver is off, so nothing was refused or rewritten in this window. The figures above cover whatever was recorded while it was on.
dashboardSavingsHintOff.description: Replaces the counts line when Data Saver is switched off, so the tiles above are not read as describing the present.

dashboardSavingsCompareHeading.message: The same sites, with Data Saver and without
dashboardSavingsCompareHeading.description: Heading of the table comparing optimized page loads against the unoptimized control sample.

dashboardSavingsCompareNoteOn.message: A $PERCENT$% sample of page loads is deliberately left unoptimized, so both columns are real page loads rather than a model. The ± is the 95% interval; a site whose interval crosses zero is left out, because a difference that could be zero is not a saving.
dashboardSavingsCompareNoteOn.description: Note above the comparison table when the control sample is running. It is the product's statement that this table is a measurement and not an estimate, and the interval rule is why a row can be missing.

dashboardSavingsCompareNoteOff.message: The unoptimized control sample is switched off, so no new comparisons are being collected. Anything below was recorded while it was on.
dashboardSavingsCompareNoteOff.description: Note above the comparison table when the control sample is switched off.

dashboardSavingsEmptyOn.message: No site has enough loads on both sides yet. A comparison needs at least five optimized loads and one unoptimized one on the same site.
dashboardSavingsEmptyOn.description: Empty state of the comparison table while the control sample is running: nothing yet, and what would be enough.

dashboardSavingsEmptyOff.message: No comparisons are on file, and none are being collected while the control sample is off.
dashboardSavingsEmptyOff.description: Empty state of the comparison table when the control sample is switched off.

dashboardSavingsColumnSite.description: Column header in the comparison table: the site being compared.

dashboardSavingsColumnWith.description: Column header in the comparison table: mean bytes of a page load with Data Saver on. Kept short; the heading above the table supplies "with Data Saver and without".

dashboardSavingsColumnWithout.description: Column header in the comparison table: mean bytes of a page load in the unoptimized control sample.

dashboardSavingsColumnSavedPerLoad.description: Column header in the comparison table: the difference between the two means, with its interval.

dashboardSavingsColumnLoads.description: Column header in the comparison table: how many page loads each side is based on.

dashboardSavingsLoadsCellTitle.description: Tooltip on the Loads cell, saying which side of the slash is which. Lower case, matching the cell it explains.

dashboardSavedPerLoad.description: Saved-per-load cell in the comparison table. The spread is never dropped: it is what stops the difference being read as precise.

dashboardSavedPerLoadHeavier.description: Saved-per-load cell when optimized loads came out heavier than the control ones. A negative result is reported as it stands rather than hidden.

dashboardSavingsDetailsSummary.description: Summary line of the collapsed disclosure under the Data Saver results panel.

dashboardSavingsExplainer.message: Three different kinds of number, kept apart. A page-load comparison is the difference between two sets of real loads, from the control sample above. An observed original is arithmetic: the size of the un-rewritten variant, seen before, minus what the smaller one cost now. An estimate is the size model's guess at a request that was refused before it had a size, and it is the only one of the three that depends on this extension's own arithmetic about bytes that never arrived.
dashboardSavingsExplainer.description: Body of the disclosure under the Data Saver results panel. It separates a measurement, an arithmetic subtraction and a model's guess, in that order of confidence. The three must stay distinguishable in translation — collapsing any two of them into the same wording is the failure this paragraph exists to prevent.

dashboardErrorReadSavings.description: Shown beside the Data Saver results heading when the request to the worker fails.

dashboardPlanTitle.description: Heading of the panel showing the data plan and where the billing cycle stands.

dashboardPlanNote.description: Note beside the Plan and cycle heading: how far into the billing cycle today is.

dashboardPlanUsedSince.description: Headline figure of the Plan and cycle panel when no plan size has been set, so there is nothing to show a share against.

dashboardPlanNoPlanHint.message: No plan set, so there is nothing to measure that against. Given a plan size, this becomes how much of the cycle is spent, how much a day the rest of it allows, and where the cycle ends at the current rate.
dashboardPlanNoPlanHint.description: Hint in the Plan and cycle panel when no plan size is set. It says what the panel will say once it can, rather than rendering the plan as zero.

dashboardCycleNoteCalendar.message: The cycle above runs from the calendar month. Most carrier cycles do not reset on the 1st, and a figure anchored to the wrong day is never the figure on the bill.
dashboardCycleNoteCalendar.description: Hint in the Plan and cycle panel when the cycle is anchored to the calendar month.

dashboardCycleNoteDay.message: The cycle above runs from the $DAY$ of the month. Most carrier cycles do not reset on the 1st, and a figure anchored to the wrong day is never the figure on the bill.
dashboardCycleNoteDay.description: Hint in the Plan and cycle panel when the cycle is anchored to a chosen day of the month. A whole separate message from dashboardCycleNoteCalendar so the anchor is never a fragment spliced mid-sentence.

dashboardPlanSetLink.description: Link from the Plan and cycle panel to the settings page.

dashboardPlanFigure.description: Headline figure of the Plan and cycle panel: bytes used in this cycle against the plan size.

dashboardPlanMeterNote.description: Note under the plan's progress meter: the share spent and when the cycle rolls over.

dashboardDayCountOne.description: Number of days left in the cycle, singular. Substituted into dashboardPlanRemaining.

dashboardDayCountOther.description: Number of days left in the cycle, plural. Substituted into dashboardPlanRemaining; paired with dashboardDayCountOne.

dashboardPlanRemaining.message: $LEFT$ left. Spread evenly over the $DAYS$ remaining, that is $PERDAY$ a day.
dashboardPlanRemaining.description: Hint in the Plan and cycle panel. Division, not a forecast: it says what an even spread would allow, which is a fact about the plan rather than a claim about the days ahead.

dashboardPlanSpent.message: The plan is spent. Everything from here is over it.
dashboardPlanSpent.description: Hint in the Plan and cycle panel when the whole plan has been used.

dashboardPlanEnforced.message: A limit over Everything matches this plan, so alerts fire at 75%, 90% and 100% of it and requests are refused past 100%.
dashboardPlanEnforced.description: Hint in the Plan and cycle panel when a limit covering all sites matches the plan size. "Everything" is the displayed name of the all-sites limit; translate it the same way it is translated there.

dashboardPlanMismatch.message: The limit over Everything is set to $LIMIT$, and your plan is $PLAN$. Alerts and enforcement follow the limit, not the plan.
dashboardPlanMismatch.description: Hint in the Plan and cycle panel when an all-sites limit exists but is a different size from the plan. "Everything" is the displayed name of the all-sites limit.

dashboardPlanUnenforced.message: Nothing is enforcing this plan. A limit over Everything is what turns it into alerts at 75%, 90% and 100%, and into refused requests past 100%.
dashboardPlanUnenforced.description: Hint in the Plan and cycle panel when a plan size is set but no all-sites limit exists, so the plan is a number that refuses nothing. "Everything" is the displayed name of the all-sites limit.

dashboardPlanAlignSet.description: Button that changes the existing all-sites limit to match the plan size.

dashboardPlanAlignCreate.description: Button that creates an all-sites limit matching the plan size.

dashboardWindowMismatch.message: The two windows do not line up: the limit's allowance resets on $LIMITDAY$ and your cycle resets on $CYCLEDAY$. A monthly limit runs on the calendar month, so what it refuses against is the calendar month's total, not this cycle's.
dashboardWindowMismatch.description: Hint in the Plan and cycle panel when the all-sites limit's window and the billing cycle roll over on different days, so the two dates on screen mean different things.

dashboardAnnouncePlanAligned.message: Everything is now limited to $PLAN$ a month.
dashboardAnnouncePlanAligned.description: Announced to a screen reader after an all-sites limit is created or changed to match the plan.

dashboardErrorSetLimit.description: Shown and announced when creating the all-sites limit from the Plan and cycle panel fails.

dashboardErrorReadCycle.description: Shown beside the Plan and cycle heading when the request to the worker fails.

dashboardStorageTitle.description: Heading of the panel listing what the extension has written to disk.

dashboardStorageLink.description: Link from the storage panel to the data section of the settings page.

dashboardStorageFlushError.message: Some measurements were not written to disk. The last failure was $WHEN$: $MESSAGE$. Totals from around then are lower than the traffic they describe.
dashboardStorageFlushError.description: Shown in the storage panel when a write to the database failed. This is the only surface that can admit a rejected write, so the last sentence — that the totals are understated — must survive translation.

dashboardStorageDailyTotals.description: Row label in the storage table: one row per day.

dashboardStorageHourlyTotals.description: Row label in the storage table: one row per hour.

dashboardStorageHostDetail.description: Row label in the storage table: per-hostname rows.

dashboardStoragePageLoads.description: Row label in the storage table: one row per recorded page load.

dashboardStorageSizeModel.description: Row label in the storage table: the mean sizes the extension learned, used to estimate a request that arrived with no size.

dashboardStorageBaselines.description: Row label in the storage table: sizes of un-rewritten images, which is what makes a measured saving a subtraction.

dashboardStorageNotReported.description: Value in the storage table when the worker did not send a count for that store. Lower case, matching the other values in the column.

dashboardStorageDiskInUse.description: Row label in the storage table: bytes the extension's storage occupies.

dashboardStorageDiskUnknown.description: Value in the storage table when the browser gives no figure for disk use.

dashboardStorageNote.message: Page-load rows hold the site and the origin, never a path or a query. Original image sizes are capped by count rather than by age, so they are the one store a shorter retention setting does not shorten.
dashboardStorageNote.description: Note under the storage table. Both sentences are privacy claims about what is and is not kept, and the second is an exception to the retention setting.

dashboardRowCountOne.description: Row count in the storage table, singular.

dashboardRowCountOther.description: Row count in the storage table, plural. Paired with dashboardRowCountOne.

dashboardKeyCountOne.description: Key count in the storage table, singular. These stores are keyed maps rather than row tables.

dashboardKeyCountOther.description: Key count in the storage table, plural. Paired with dashboardKeyCountOne.

dashboardErrorReadStorage.description: Shown in the storage panel when the request to the worker fails.

dashboardErrorReadSeries.message: Could not read the daily series.
dashboardErrorReadSeries.description: Announced when the daily chart's request to the worker fails.

dashboardErrorReadUsage.description: Shown in place of the stat cards, and announced, when the overview request to the worker fails.
